A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PRInTS study. Their complete main text, Appendices A–B, equations, tables and figures support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original agent evaluations on FRAMES, GAIA and WebWalkerQA, alongside ablations and scaling experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds annotation-stability, annotator-capacity and failure analyses in Appendix B.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 and Figure 3 drop v1's requirement that the initial winning candidate follow the shortest successful trajectory; v2 specifies a successful trajectory. This revises the stated annotation procedure, without establishing that data were regenerated. The architecture, rewards, summarization and inference procedure otherwise remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The Alibaba/MiroVerse training sources and FRAMES, GAIA and WebWalkerQA task coverage are retained. New diagnostics reuse source queries and existing GAIA subsets. Multilingual evaluation remains future work.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their respective comparator sets, including GenPRM-7B, Web-Shepherd-8B and StepWiser. The scaling and separate-summarizer comparisons also remain. Qwen3-14B appears in an annotation-policy capacity ablation, without introducing a competing PRM method.

E3.justification: Appendix B adds diagnostics on 400 source queries, varying annotation rollout budgets and comparing Qwen3-32B with Qwen3-14B at M=8. Figure 4's caption changes the reported agent from Qwen3-32B to Tongyi DeepResearch-30B-A3B, while the accompanying text still names Qwen3-32B. This is an inconsistent setting revision, not evidence of a rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained context, reward, summarizer and scaling ablations, Appendix B adds annotation-noise validation, annotator-capacity sensitivity and qualitative failure analysis on GAIA Levels 2–3. These substantially broaden scrutiny of supervision reliability and failure behavior, including rejection of the correct answer 'mice' for insufficient evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report Avg@3 over three independent evaluation runs. v2 additionally introduces 1,000 bootstrap resamples at smaller rollout budgets against an M=32 pseudo-ground-truth reference, reporting estimation variance, MAE and preference-flip rates. This adds substantive uncertainty analysis without establishing additional runs of the original benchmark evaluations.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 and existing performance curves retain their values. Appendix B adds focused diagnostic results: variance of 0.025, 0.011 and 0.004 at M=4,8,16; preference-flip rates of 3.62% and 1.81% at M=4,16; and 240 versus 169 preference pairs from the 32B versus 14B annotator. It also reports the new correct-answer rejection case.

T1.justification: The trajectory, information-gain and reward definitions remain mathematically equivalent. Scorer and summarizer equations move inline, and the comparison reward is reformatted. The half-point increment explanation and new reward-computation example illustrate existing mathematics; no new theorem, proof or substantive derivation appears.

C1.justification: The dual-capability contribution and cross-agent improvement claims remain. The Introduction narrows the specific OpenAI DeepResearch comparison: the unchanged 64.4% GAIA result now 'closes the gap' to 67.4%, instead of matching it. The comparison with DeepSeek-V3.1's reported 63.1% gains explicit emphasis on model size.

C2.justification: v2 adds English-language and agent-training scope limitations, explains the relationship between annotator capability and pair yield, and makes the factual-grounding versus trajectory-efficiency tradeoff explicit. It expands the existing overexploration explanation. Section 4.1 also adds a stronger memory/computation advantage claim over the 671B reference model without a direct cost comparison.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly reports training hardware and duration: eight RTX 6000 Ada GPUs with 48GB each, approximately 0.5 hours per SFT epoch and 3.5 per GRPO epoch, totaling 16 hours. Existing hyperparameters, prompts and access links remain. The main text introduces an unresolved 'X iterations' placeholder, although Appendix A retains four cycles.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to agent fine-tuning, generative PRMs and context compression remain substantively unchanged. Related-work prose is condensed and bibliography formatting changes, but no cited research work is added or removed.

P1.justification: The main text is extensively condensed and rewritten across related work, methods, experimental descriptions and discussion. Experimental Setup is folded into Section 4, benchmark and metric descriptions are combined, and Limitations and Ethical Considerations sections are added. The acronym expansion changes from 'Progress Reward' to 'Process Reward'.

P2.justification: Paper-wide reformatting changes the title/author block, typography, column geometry, headers and caption styling. v2 adds the reward-computation Figure 7 and places the retained preference-pair figure beneath it. Existing tables and plots largely preserve their display structures, while appendix figures are resized, relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: Appendix B adds useful evidence about previously unquantified annotation noise and annotator choice, together with a concrete failure analysis. Training-resource disclosure and the more accurate OpenAI comparison also improve transparency. These gains outweigh the editorial problems, but the Figure 4 model mismatch, 'X iterations' placeholder and unmeasured stronger inference-efficiency claim limit the improvement.
